speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what is the extent of MAS’ regulatory oversight of the Central Depository Pte Ltd (CDP) and its relationships and obligations towards individual customers; (b) what avenues for assistance are available for CDP customers who are not digitally literate or savvy, including persons whose accounts have been suspended; and (c) whether MAS considers these avenues adequate in light of some CDP customers being of elderly age and not digitally literate.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have got two supplementary questions on behalf of my Clementi residents.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: We have Clementi residents, such as those from Faber Hills in Clementi, who are elderly and prefer face-to-face interactions and are still quite worried about access to counter service when transacting with the CDP.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, the first question is, whether the standard of service prescribed is different compared to a retail bank which, like CDP, would have many legacy customers who are older and not so digitally-savvy?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: My second question, pertains to whether or not the customers who are sent digital notices to provide information to keep their accounts open – do these customers also receive telephone calls or paper, physical letters if they do not respond?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I ask this because I have a Clementi resident, a retired stockbroker, his CDP trading account was suspended because he did not use the online system to update his particulars.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: My resident says he is not computer literate, does not own a personal computer.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, can the Minister of State confirm whether CDP's practices include telephone and paper physical letter outreach before someone's trading account is suspended, due to potential implications if they need to access that account urgently at a future date?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng has been speaking very passionately about CDP and he has raised many of these discrete cases with me, such as the ones on CDP account openings and suspensions, as well as access to CDP digital services.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Both Dr Tan and I have been working on these cases on behalf of his Clementi residents.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On his first point, I had mentioned in my earlier reply that MAS expects all MAS-licensed financial institutions to treat customers fairly – including all of the effective support and feedback channels.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I also want to commend the Member on many of his suggestions over the years.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Just to update him on a few aspects, in which there have been enhancements to CDP as a result of MAS engagements with CDP to avail more in-person channels to those that are less digitally-literate.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: One point to note is that at least 99% of all CDP customers access its services digitally or over calls.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, that means that a vast majority are digitally-savvy.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But as the Member knows, the Government's position is that we are not going to be digital-only but, we want to adopt a digital-first approach.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Therefore, CDP has made a couple of different enhancements over the years.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First, CDP now grants in-person appointments via the SGX Vista premises.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Second, CDP now provides instant video conferencing services with CDP service representatives.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: CDP has also published user guides and instructional videos on the Internet and social media.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There is also a new chatbot on SGX's website.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That said, there are always scope for improvements to CDP's customer journey, including and particularly, for those that are less digitally-savvy.
